# devflow

> Isolated dev environments for every Git workspace — worktrees, databases, caches, and stateful services that sync with your Git workflow.

devflow gives each Git workspace its own isolated development environment. Running
`devflow switch -c feature-auth` creates (or switches to) a dedicated worktree and
service instances that belong to that workspace. Select code and data origins
independently; local providers use Copy-on-Write where the filesystem supports it.

## Automation defaults

- Always pass `--json --non-interactive` for machine-safe execution.
- Use `--non-interactive` on `switch` to run lifecycle hooks without prompts; unapproved shell hooks are skipped unless pre-approved.
- Use `devflow --json capabilities` to detect automation guarantees at runtime.
- Use `devflow --json doctor --strict` as a CI/agent health gate; inspect `summary` and `next_steps` for remediation.
- Non-zero exit code means failure; partial multi-provider failures also return non-zero.
- Note: `--no-verify` skips ALL hooks entirely — only use when hooks are genuinely unwanted.
- Git uses linked worktrees for every additional workspace; jj uses native workspaces.
- Consume raw `name`, reported `service_key`, and `worktree_path` from `devflow --json list`; never reconstruct legacy keys.
- Use `switch -c task --from main --data-from baseline:clean@v1` to choose independent code and data origins.
- Use `baseline prepare NAME --service SERVICE --from FILE` to seal reusable local PostgreSQL data.
- Use `exec --workspace TASK -- PROGRAM ARGS` for literal arguments; use `--shell` for shell syntax.
- Inspect saved operations with `operation list --history` and `operation inspect ID`; resume supported operations with `operation resume ID`.
- Check `operation.status` before starting dependent work: `ready` confirms setup; `needs_attention` requires inspecting skipped or failed phases.
- Retry incomplete setup with the same command. `doctor` reports pending operations; failed seeds require a successful seed retry.
- Run `remove` from a different workspace; current/default workspaces remain protected even with `--force`.

## Docs

- [README.md](README.md): Product overview, quickstart, configuration reference, CLI reference, and install guide.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): Agent-first onboarding, bootstrap flow, suggested agent loop, and automation contract.
- [Data baselines](docs-site/src/content/docs/guides/baselines.md): Prepare sealed PostgreSQL generations and reset children to a recorded version.
- [Retention and caches](docs-site/src/content/docs/guides/retention-and-caches.md): Pins, expiry, cleanup plans and fingerprinted artifact reuse.
- [Provider catalog](docs-site/src/content/docs/reference/provider-catalog.md): Generated operation capabilities and required configuration.
- [Ownership and recovery](docs-site/src/content/docs/guides/ownership-and-recovery.md): Independent code/data origins, resource migration, readiness, and recovery.
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): Project structure, config schema, development commands, and AI agent context.
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): Version history and release notes.
- [Documentation site](https://clement-tourriere.github.io/devflow/): Full documentation site (Astro Starlight; source in docs-site/).

## Agent workflows

- [examples/agent-bootstrap.sh](examples/agent-bootstrap.sh): Idempotent repository setup for agents and CI; initializes config, hooks, and agent guide files.
- [examples/agent-task.sh](examples/agent-task.sh): Create/switch to a task-scoped workspace and emit a JSON handoff object with agent_workdir and connection info.
- [scripts/release-check.sh](scripts/release-check.sh): Local release-candidate verification gate for formatting, tests, builds, and generated guidance.
- [examples/simple.devflow.yml](examples/simple.devflow.yml): Minimal single-service configuration.
- [examples/multi-service.devflow.yml](examples/multi-service.devflow.yml): Multi-service setup with hooks and worktrees.
- [examples/django.devflow.yml](examples/django.devflow.yml): Django project config with migrations and Docker Compose.

## Source (for code agents)

- [src/cli/mod.rs](src/cli/mod.rs): Command routing, JSON/non-interactive behavior, multi-provider orchestration.
- [crates/devflow-core/src/agent.rs](crates/devflow-core/src/agent.rs): AI agent integration (skill generation, context, rules).
- [crates/devflow-core/src/config/mod.rs](crates/devflow-core/src/config/mod.rs): Config loading, 3-tier merging, env var overrides, validation.
- [crates/devflow-core/src/services/mod.rs](crates/devflow-core/src/services/mod.rs): `ServiceProvider` trait — the interface all providers implement.
- [crates/devflow-core/src/services/factory.rs](crates/devflow-core/src/services/factory.rs): Provider creation, dispatch, multi-provider orchestration.
- [crates/devflow-core/src/hooks/executor.rs](crates/devflow-core/src/hooks/executor.rs): Hook execution engine, approval checks, conditions.
- [crates/devflow-core/src/hooks/template.rs](crates/devflow-core/src/hooks/template.rs): MiniJinja template engine with custom filters.
- [crates/devflow-core/src/vcs/mod.rs](crates/devflow-core/src/vcs/mod.rs): VCS abstraction (Git + Jujutsu), auto-detection.
- [crates/devflow-core/src/services/plugin.rs](crates/devflow-core/src/services/plugin.rs): Plugin provider protocol (JSON-over-stdio).

## Optional

- [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt): Comprehensive agent context (all commands, config schema, hook phases).
